target_claim: Proof 2's injectivity step asserts, for arbitrary a in S, that for all x_1, x_2 in S, (x_1, a circ x_1) in lambda_a AND (x_2, a circ x_2) in lambda_a implies x_1 = x_2. Since (x, a circ x) belongs to lambda_a for EVERY x by the definition of lambda_a, the antecedent is universally satisfied, so the stated claim literally asserts that S has at most one element. The preceding chain x_1 = a * lambda_a(x_1) = a * lambda_a(x_2) = x_2 uses an unjustified middle equality (many-to-one-ness of lambda_a only gives single-valuedness at a fixed argument, not lambda_a(x_1) = lambda_a(x_2)).
source_quote: :$\forall x_1, x_2 \in S: (x_1, a \circ x_1) \in \lambda_a \wedge  (x_2, a \circ x_2) \in \lambda_a \implies x_1 = x_2$
